label: Codex-gpt-5.6-sol-reviewer2-fulltext-2026-10-03

country.paper_says: The study concerns the Portuguese water and waste sector and states that “All the 278 municipalities of mainland Portugal are covered.”

study_design.paper_says: The paper uses 2011 municipal data to perform quantitative comparisons among a no-social-tariff baseline, actual social tariffs, and synthetic R1/09 tariffs. It states: “The reference year is 2011 and the municipality is the relevant unit of analysis.”

population.paper_says: “The reference year is 2011 and the municipality is the relevant unit of analysis. All the 278 municipalities of mainland Portugal are covered.”

sample_size.paper_says: A sample size can be extracted: 278 municipalities for the all-municipality water-provision analysis. Service-specific actual-ST samples were 101 municipalities for water provision, 77 for wastewater treatment, and 68 for undifferentiated waste management.
sample_size.where: p. 11, Scope of Analysis; p. 17, Table 3; p. 19, Table 6

urban_rural.paper_says: The analysis covers all mainland municipalities, and the paper explicitly refers to municipalities classified as “mainly urban, somewhat urban and mainly rural,” supporting a mixed setting.

service_provider.paper_says: The paper reports “357 economically regulated providers,” of which 338 retail-service operators were considered; this “translates into the total 278 municipalities for WP and WT and only 258 for UWM.” The 278 figure therefore refers to municipalities, not 278 providers. The three management models are direct management, municipalised services, and private concessions.
service_provider.where: p. 4, The Sector; p. 6, Water; p. 11, Scope of Analysis

regulatory_model.paper_says: R1/09 and Recommendation no. 2/2010 are both non-binding guidelines, but the social-tariff scenarios studied are based specifically on R1/09. The paper says R1/09 is “simply a set of guidelines,” while the conclusion identifies evaluating the combined effect of R1/09 and Recommendation no. 2/2010 as future work; R2/10 concerns tariff-calculation criteria rather than the analyzed social-tariff design.
regulatory_model.where: pp. 2–3, Introduction; p. 8, ERSAR; p. 23, Conclusion

effect_measure.paper_says: The methodology compares S0 (no social tariffs), S1 (actual social tariffs), and S2 (R1/09 social tariffs), reporting measures including “Total subsidy volume,” “Subsidy per beneficiary,” and bill accrual for non-beneficiaries.

effect_estimate.paper_says: The broad conclusions and EUR 19.11 average, EUR 2.53–40.52 range, and EUR 37.99 spread are supported. However, existing social tariffs were not quantified across all 278 municipalities: actual-ST samples were 101 municipalities for WP, 77 for WT, and 68 for UWM. For all 278 municipalities, the analysis compares the no-ST baseline with synthetic R1/09 tariffs using potential users. The study also assumes the upper-bound threshold of EUR 13,580 rather than treating it merely as a cap.
effect_estimate.where: p. 5, Table 2; pp. 8–9, Concept of Social Tariffs; p. 17, Table 3; pp. 17–19, Methodology and Table 6

extraction_note.paper_says: The paper itself does not contain the review-system identifier “RA7E07382F0E4.”

parsed.overall_comment: Most high-level descriptors are supported, but the service-provider and effect-estimate entries conflate municipalities with providers and overstate the coverage of the actual-social-tariff analysis. R2/10 was contextual and proposed for future combined analysis, whereas the modeled social-tariff recommendation was R1/09.
